newsitem.title: USA: Three movies battle for top honors at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Three movies battle for top honors at U.S. box office.

text.p: Three movies were tied for the top position at the U.S. box office over Superbowl weekend as the studios engaged in some bitter rivalry while they tried to estimate how the football match would affect film grosses.

According to Exhibitor Relations, which collects the studios' data, reigning champion "Beverly Hills Ninja," "Jerry Maguire," and newcomer "In Love and War" each earned an estimated $5.9 million during the Friday-to-Sunday period.
The Eddie Murphy vehicle "Metro" slipped two notches to fourth place in its second weekend with $5.6 million, and the musical "Evita" was also down two to fifth and $5.5 million.

Exhibitor Relations said the difficulty of estimating the extent to which people would stay home Sunday to watch the game on television rather than go to the movies meant rankings were certain to change when final data are released Monday.

However several studios were wasting no time criticizing their rivals' estimates. Walt Disney Co., which released "Metro," believed its movie was tied for first with Sony Corp's "Jerry Maguire" and they each made $5.6 million.
However, if Sony was estimating $5.9 million for "Maguire," then Disney would do so for "Metro," said Phil Barlow, president of Disney's Buena Vista distribution arm.
"On a weekend that no one picture made $6 million, it seems ludicrous to have an 'I can top that contest,'" said Barlow. A Sony spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
Barlow estimated "Metro" made $4.52 million on Friday and Saturday, while "Jerry Maguire" made $4.49 million and "Beverly Hills Ninja" made $4.25 million.

New Line Cinema, which releases "In Love and War," does not break out day-to-day estimates, said a spokesman for the Time Warner Inc.-owned studio. The World War I romance movie stars Chris O'Donnell as Ernest Hemingway and Sandra Bullock as the nurse he fell in love with. Its attraction to females means it has a "much stronger playability" during the Superbowl weekend than male-skewing movies such as "Metro" or "Beverly Hills Ninja," the spokesman said.
Barlow predicted "Evita," another female-oriented movie, and "In Love And War" would end up with about $5.4 million for the weekend, a little behind "Beverly Hills Ninja."

The Superbowl impact is hard to gauge, although 80 percent of the weekend gross comes from the Friday and Saturday of a Superbowl weekend, industry officials said. The percentage is usually in the 70s on other weekends. The calculation is complicated by the "time shift" factor as people opt to see a movie Friday or Saturday in order to leave Sunday free.
Among the overall totals, "Jerry Maguire" has $110.2 million, "Beverly Hills Ninja" has $19.4 million, "Metro" has $18.9 million and "Evita" has $30.6 million.

Somewhat overshadowed were the rather disappointing debuts of two other movies in the top 10. "Fierce Creatures," starring the cast from the hit 1988 movie "A Fish Called Wanda," opened in eighth with $4.0 million. The 10th spot went to "Zeus and Roxanne," a children's movie, with $2.9 million.

"Fierce Creatures" was released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd.. "Zeus and Roxanne" is released by MGM, which is owned by financier Kirk Kerkorian and Australia's Seven Network Ltd..
